meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mainland China and Taiwan area both apply civil-law statutory regimes; cross-strait conflict-of-law rules govern investor documentation and dispute resolution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) - applicable in lieu of a state-to-state BIT
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2012)
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Tax Evasion on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended 2024, effective 1 January 2025); People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation (PBOC/SAMR) Order No. 3 (2024) Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Registration, effective 1 November 2024; PBOC Order No. 3 (2024) Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records Preservation; Law of the People's Republic of China on Protection of Investments by Taiwanese Compatriots and its implementing rules; Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (for Taiwan-origin fund flows).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Taiwan Investor Certificate of Incorporation and Company Registration Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Central Company Registration Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-origin instrument: Taiwan district court or contractual notary public notarization; then Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification; then Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) / designated mainland notary office verification. The Hague Apostille Convention does not apply because Taiwan is not a Hague Contracting Party. Use this exclusive cross-strait consular legalization path; never chain an apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Fact reflecting current registration status and no striking-off action
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-origin instrument: Taiwan notarization by a competent court notary or notary public; then SEF verification; then ARATS verification by the designated mainland notary association. Apostille is not permitted for Taiwan-origin documents. For documents originating from a Hague Apostille Convention state, the competent authority of that state must issue a standalone apostille; do not combine apostille with consular or cross-strait legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Taiwan Investor approving WFOE establishment, authorized capital, and appointment of legal representative / power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor board of directors or shareholders meeting
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board resolution and power of attorney must be notarized in Taiwan by a Taiwan notary public or court notary; then verified by SEF; then verified by ARATS-designated mainland notary office. This is mandatory consular-equivalent legalization. If the same instrument were issued in a Hague Apostille state, a standalone apostille would be used; never sequence apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the Taiwan Investor (current consolidated version certified by the registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor and Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs company registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Articles must be notarized in Taiwan, SEF-verified, and ARATS-verified before acceptance by mainland SAMR, foreign-exchange bank, or tax authority. Because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention member, no apostille may be attached. The only parallel alternative applies when the originating jurisdiction is a Hague member state; in that case apostille alone is acceptable. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan Investor's issuing bank confirming corporate account conduct and beneficial owner details held by the bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-licensed bank under the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be signed by the bank's authorized officer, notarized in Taiwan, SEF-verified, and ARATS-verified for use in mainland China. This is the cross-strait consular legalization path. A Hague apostille cannot replace it when the letter originates in Taiwan. If a group parent in a Hague Contracting State issues a bank reference letter, apostille alone is the required authentication path; do not combine both paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, legal representatives, supervisors, authorized signatories and counterparties against OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; UN Security Council consolidated list; China's PBOC/SAMR prohibited and fraudulent entity lists, the Supreme People's Court judgment default list, and any domestic judicial red-list notices; Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML blacklist where relevant. PEP screening must cover current and former mainland Chinese public officials, Taiwan-area elected and appointed political figures, foreign state officials, and their family members and close associates. Screening must include fuzzy matching, phonetic and romanization variants, identification document verification, adverse media review, and look-through to natural-person beneficial owners. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP trigger or high-risk jurisdiction link even though the industry is classified Low_Risk_Standard. The UBO declaration must be updated within 30 days of any change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Registration and Reservation System (National Enterprise Registration Integrated Online Service Platform under the State Administration for Market Regulation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory Chinese company names must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business description, and organizational form, namely Limited Liability Company or Co., Ltd. The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters. Taiwan-origin traditional Chinese names must be transliterated into simplified Chinese. Pinyin romanization is accepted for English-name registration only and must not create confusion with the registered Chinese name. The English name is auxiliary and does not replace the Chinese statutory name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Taiwan when used to imply a separate sovereign state or as a standalone administrative division
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial name reservation is valid for

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan's Company Act (公司法), primarily Articles 128, 129, 154, 156, 161, 172, 192, 208, 218, and 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例) Articles 6-8; Regulations for the Approval of Foreign Investment (外國人投資條例施行細則).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業司), Taiwan, R.O.C.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司登記申請書) together with executed Articles of Incorporation and the First Board Resolutions; filed through the One-Stop Business Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None across the board for general WFOE in the digital software sector; however, if bank escrow is used to evidence capital transfer, the escrow account is blocked until the Company Registration Certificate is issued. The paid-up capital must be deposited in a Taiwan bank account under the company's name; no minimum amount is statutorily fixed for ISIC 6201 activities. The capital injection is verified via a CPA capital confirmation report submitted in the registration dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD. HELD AT [Registered Office Address], Taiwan, on [Date] at [Time], upon due notice in accordance with Article 204 of the Company Act. Present: all founding directors and the shareholder representative of the sole foreign investor, holding 100% of the issued shares. The Chairperson declared a quorum present and presided over the meeting. The Board, having reviewed the Articles of Incorporation and the investment approval certificate, adopted the following resolutions unanimously. 1. SHARE CAPITAL: RESOLVED, that the issued share capital of the Company be fixed at [Currency][Amount], divided into [Number] ordinary shares with par value of [Currency][Amount] each; that the shares be fully subscribed and paid up by the sole shareholder; and that the capital be deposited into a bank account designated by the Company and verified by certified public accountants prior to registration. 2. BANKING: RESOLVED, that the Company open demand deposit and foreign currency accounts with [Bank Name] in Taiwan; that the Chairperson, Managing Director, and General Manager, acting jointly in any two, be and are hereby authorized to sign all payment instructions, checks, and banking agreements; and that payment below [Threshold] may be signed singly by the General Manager. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business be located at [Registered Office Address], Taiwan, and that the Company adopt this address for all statutory notices and service of process. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chairperson and legal representative, [Name] be appointed Managing Director, [Name] be appointed General Manager, and [Name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer; that the Company Secretary be responsible for maintaining the corporate seal and share registers; and that the Chairperson be authorized to execute the Company Registration Application and all ancillary documents. 5. GOVERNANCE: RESOLVED, that the Chairperson convene annual general meetings within six months of each fiscal year-end; that the board meet at least once per quarter; and that internal audit procedures compliant with the Company Act be adopted. 6. AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and Company Secretary are authorized to file the registration, pay official fees, receive the Certificate of Incorporation, and do all things necessity to effectuate these resolutions. PASSED unanimously and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (投審會) and Department of Commercial Affairs (for name reservation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must submit a Foreign Investment Application through the Investment Commission's online portal, including the business plan, identity and incorporation documents of the foreign company, audited financial statements, power of attorney appointing a local agent, and a declaration of no conflict with negative list items. The application is reviewed for compliance with the Foreign Investment Act. Upon approval, the investor obtains an Investment Approval Letter. In parallel, the Taiwan entity name and business scope are reserved via the Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System. The proposed name must end with 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The name reservation is valid for six months. The submission must be made after verifying the Shanghai or Taiwan trade register number of the parent company and confirming the exact ISIC 6201 software classification.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the investor's certificate of incorporation or equivalent
Audited financial statements of the investor (last fiscal year)
Power of attorney appointing a Taiwan resident agent
Detailed business plan and product/service description
Declaration of non-involvement in prohibited industries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, the applicant has 30 days to file supplementary explanations or corrected documents; if the name is rejected, the applicant may re-reserve a new name and appeal the rejection through the administrative appeal process within 30 days of receiving the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Injunction and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank in Taiwan and licensed CPA (會計師)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After investment approval, the foreign shareholder must remit the subscribed paid-up capital from an overseas account into a Taiwan bank account opened in the name of the yet-to-be-registered company (pre-registration account) or into a temporary escrow account held by the law firm. The remittance must be evidenced by a bank receipt showing currency conversion into New Taiwan Dollars (TWD). The company retains a licensed CPA to issue a Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告), confirming that the capital has been actually paid and that no portion is borrowed or subject to refundation. The CPA will check the bank statement, currency exchange record, and the shareholder's remittance instruction. The CPA report is a mandatory annex to the incorporation filing. The capital cannot be withdrawn or used for operating expenses until the company registration certificate is obtained and the escrow is released according to the bank's instruction.
required_dossiers: CPA engagement letter and capital verification certificate
Share subscription list and payment schedule
Escrow agreement if capital is held by a law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA refuses to issue the report due to insufficient capital documentation, the investor must provide additional bank confirmation or convert the currency within 10 days; if the remittance is stuck in customs or bank compliance, a corrected remittance instruction may be submitted and the SLA restarts from receipt of the verified funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (via One-Stop Business Registration Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Taiwan agent or attorney must login to the One-Stop Business Registration Portal, complete the Company Registration Application, upload the Articles of Incorporation, the First Board Resolutions, the share register, the CPA capital verification report, the investment approval letter, and the address proof for the registered office. The system calculates registration fees and permits online payment. The authority reviews the filed documents for statutory consistency, particularly the company name, business scope, directors, and capital. If all conditions are met, the Ministry issues the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書). The certificate contains the company's unified business tax number (統一編號). The registration is public and the company becomes a legal person from the date of issuance. The certificate is the foundational document for opening permanent bank accounts and signing commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Registered office address consent form and lease
ID/passport copies of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for corrections, the applicant has 15 business days to file revisions; if the certificate is suspended because of a dispute over business scope, the applicant must file an amended application with a revised scope; an administrative appeal may be filed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days after the suspension notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau (國稅局) under the Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the company registration certificate is obtained, the company must apply for business registration (營業登記) with the local National Taxation Bureau. The application must include the registration certificate, articles of incorporation, and director ID. The bureau issues the Unified Business Number (統一編號) if not already assigned, and the company is enrolled in the Business Tax ledger. The company must also register for Corporate Income Tax filings, Business Tax (value-added tax) filings, and the Uniform Invoice (統一發票) scheme. The tax authority may inspect the registered office to confirm actual business presence. After this step, the company may issue uniform invoices and purchase invoices. For a software company, no special VAT exemption applies unless the software qualifies as exported services; the standard Business Tax rate is 5%. Employment health insurance and labor insurance registrations are separate but often triggered through the same portal.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution appointing the tax representative
Lease contract for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau requests site inspection and finds no physical office, the company may submit a telecommunication-based service description and a letter of authorization from the landlord; if tax registration is delayed, the company may be subject to late filing penalties, but the company can apply for a waiver based on force majeure or official delay with written evidence within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and EFOS Invoicing Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank and the National Taxation Bureau's Invoice system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number, the company opens permanent bank accounts at the chosen bank. The original bank activation requires the corporate seal, the legal representative's identification, and a board resolution authorizing signatories. The bank performs AML/KYC checks; for a WFOE in software, the risk tier is standard low risk. Additionally, the company applies for the Electronic Uniform Invoicing System (電子統一發票) via the tax bureau's online portal to issue e-invoices for B2B and B2C transactions. If the company intents to accept Stripe Billing or direct debit, the bank account must be cable-enabled for foreign currency receipts and settlement. The company also obtains a VAT certificate and may apply for an export service zero-rated or exemption declaration if the software provision qualifies as international service.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal and legal representative ID
First Board Resolution on banking and invoicing
Proof of investment approval and CPA capital report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete beneficial ownership information, the company must provide a full corporate chain chart and source of funds documentation; if the e-invoice application is rejected, the company must apply for paper uniform invoices instead and later re-apply for e-invoice within 6 months.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Pure digital/cloud software service (ISIC 6201) with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing activity; no EIA report, environmental registration, or permit required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - The enterprise does not generate wastewater, VOC emissions, hazardous waste, or industrial discharges. General office waste is handled by municipal collection. If cloud data centers are used, they are operated by third-party Tier III/IV providers fully compliant with their own environmental permits; the WFOE does not own or operate such facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - No Civil Defense fire permit or factory inspection is required for a software company operating in a leased class A/B office building. The company must nevertheless comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by maintaining fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and safety signage; the landlord is responsible for the building's structural load and primary fire-safety certification. The local fire department may inspect the office after a complaint; the company should keep a basic self-inspection record and fire evacuation plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) unified tax service platform (etax.chinatax.gov.cn); for customs/export declarations the China International Trade Single Window under the General Administration of Customs is the complementary electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A CN_WFOE_LTD is a resident PRC limited liability company, so the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the business license issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Procedure: (1) complete company formation and obtain the SAMR business license; (2) within 30 days of license issuance, log onto the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax), complete the taxpayer registration, and receive the USCC-based tax account and tax office assignment; (3) if the expected annual taxable sales will exceed CNY 5,000,000, or if customers require general taxpayer VAT invoices, apply for general VAT taxpayer registration through e-Tax before issuing VAT invoices; (4) register the export VAT exemption/zero-rating profile in the export tax refund module for cross-border software exports; (5) a Taiwan-resident parent shareholder is not issued a PRC TIN by this process; for non-resident withholding purposes the parent must deliver its Taiwan tax registration/TIN and, where treaty benefits are claimed, a Taiwan Tax Resident Certificate to the PRC withholding agent. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a PRC establishment earning China-source income does not receive a PRC TIN; the payer files non-resident withholding via e-Tax using the foreign enterprise's home-country tax identification number and tax residence evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections. The WFOE is taxed as a PRC resident enterprise on its worldwide income at entity level; the Taiwan shareholder is treated as a non-resident enterprise for PRC withholding tax purposes with no alternative classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2026) and its implementing regulations; the standard headline rate for goods is 13%, while software services and SaaS supplies that are not zero-rated are normally taxed at the 6% modern services VAT rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All WFOEs must complete tax registration within 30 days of obtaining the business license, regardless of turnover; there is therefore no minimum threshold for obtaining a tax registration number. For VAT classification, an enterprise with annual taxable sales above CNY 5,000,000 (approx. USD 690,000) is mandatorily a general VAT taxpayer; below that threshold, the taxpayer may remain a small-scale taxpayer subject to the small-scale levy rate, but an entity that regularly exports zero-rated services is advised to register as a general VAT taxpayer in order to claim input VAT refunds on export costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA operates the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) and the Golden Tax Project IV control system. General VAT taxpayers must issue invoices through the national e-invoice platform; FDEIs carry a tax-authority-assigned unique invoice number and anti-fraud digital fingerprint, and invoice data is transmitted to the tax authority in near real time. High-volume issuers and SaaS billing providers using Stripe Billing or Direct Debit must integrate through the STA's e-invoice API or through the e-Tax portal, with the invoice data automatically reconciled against declared VAT in the nationwide electronic invoice clearance environment. The system does not require a legacy tax-control device for FDEI taxpayers; instead, issuance, red-letter reversals, and data correction are carried out through the unified electronic invoice service platform, and any mismatch between invoicing, declared output VAT, and export refund declarations is flagged by the tax authority's risk-monitoring engine.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% VAT applies when the goods are physically exported from the PRC, an electronic Customs Export Declaration is filed through the China International Trade Single Window, and export proceeds are repatriated to a PRC designated foreign exchange bank in accordance with SAFE rules. For qualifying cloud ERP/CRM software services sold to an overseas recipient, including a Taiwan-registered legal person, the export supply is eligible for 0% VAT (and refund of attributable input VAT) when the following statutory criteria are met: (1) the WFOE is a PRC general VAT taxpayer; (2) the service recipient is a non-resident legal entity with no PRC permanent establishment; (3) the software/SaaS service is consumed wholly outside mainland China; (4) the contract or order originates outside China; (5) the consideration is received in foreign currency, or RMB through an offshore RMB clearing channel, by a PRC bank and is properly reported as cross-border service trade; and (6) the WFOE files the export VAT zero-rating/exemption declaration and attaches the service contract, overseas recipient's tax residence evidence, and the bank receipt. Pure cloud delivery does not require physical customs clearance, but any tangible storage media exported as part of the software supply must be separately documented under the customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export Bill of Entry / export customs clearance record filed through the China International Trade Single Window; required only for physical goods including exported software media)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (carrier transport document evidencing the physical export movement; not applicable to cloud-delivered SaaS)
Commercial invoice / export invoice / SaaS subscription invoice issued by the WFOE and matching the contract value

Foreign exchange receipt / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or designated-PRC-bank export proceeds settlement voucher showing the offshore/Taiwan payer's remittance and the transaction code for cross-border service trade

Cross-border service transaction evidence bundle, including the signed SaaS/ERP license agreement, the overseas recipient's business registration or tax residence certificate confirming no PRC establishment, and any bank/SAFE current-account transaction record

Export VAT zero-rating/exemption declaration and the export tax refund (exemption) e-filing package submitted through the STA export tax refund system, containing the VAT invoice, payment receipts, and contract schedules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, the provincial tax bureau, SAFE, and the General Administration of Customs carry out post-filing audits of export zero-rating claims. If the supporting documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or the foreign exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days is missed, the zero-rated treatment is reversed and the VAT becomes payable with late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day from the original due date. Where a refund/exemption is obtained by fraud, false invoicing, forged customs declarations, or fictitious cross-border service contracts, the STA will claw back the entire VAT refund and impose fines ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax underrecovered or refunded, in addition to the late-payment surcharge; serious cases involving fraudulent export tax refunds are prosecuted as criminal tax fraud under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which may result in criminal fines, forfeiture, and imprisonment. Retrospective adjustments are generally assessed for the statutory three-year tax collection period, extended to five or more years in cases of evasion or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China's foreign exchange control is a managed float with conditional RMB convertibility. Current-account items, including software/CRM service exports, royalties and infrastructure cost recharges, are generally convertible through designated banks upon presentation of genuine transactions, without SAFE pre-approval in routine cases. The capital account remains subject to SAFE registration and case-by-case supervision: inbound equity contributed by the Taiwan shareholder, foreign debt, dividends, profit repatriation, and liquidation proceeds require a traceable FDI record, a designated foreign currency settlement account and verifiable source-of-funds documentation. Conversion of repatriated equity or trade FX into RMB follows payment-purpose settlement, not free market convertibility; banks record each receipt and the economic purpose. Repatriation of audited post-tax profits to Taiwan is lawful only after payment of corporate income tax, withholding tax if applicable, and submission of annual audit plus stamp-tax clearance. Practically, a China WFOE can open an export-foreign-currency settlement account, retain USD/EUR receipts for operating payments, and hedge using SAFE-approved FX products. However, capital outflows not tied to real commerce are blocked; cross-border netting and internal treasury concentration must be documented and booked with a bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Post-2012 regulatory framework: no uniform surrender percentage is applied to export proceeds. A mainland WFOE may retain incoming foreign currency in its current-account FX settlement account or convert to RMB as needed. The binding obligations are (1) all export proceeds for goods and services must be repatriated to a SAFE-licensed bank before the contractual payment due date, and for goods no later than 90 days after the customs declaration date; for digital services no later than 30 days after the invoice or deliverable date if payment terms are shorter; (2) proceeds may not be deposited or netted offshore without SAFE authorisation; and (3) if the total export collection ratio under SAFE's annual verification falls below the bank's threshold, the bank may require conversion of every subsequent remittance to RMB until the ratio is restored. For this WFOE, presume a 0% fixed conversion ratio, but do not retain export proceeds without an underlying recorded account, invoice and clearing rail.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Unviable as a primary treasury bank; narrow viability as a cross-border collection and payment-service-provider complement under PBOC real-name controls. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut or other multi-currency fintech platforms are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE as deposit-taking institutions and cannot hold RMB accounts, process capital injections, or furnish a bank-confirmed ledger for SAFE annual inspections. A WFOE may use foreign PSPs to collect USD/EUR subscription fees, but settlement must funnel into a licensed bank FX settlement account via a PBOC-registered cross-border payment institution. Any attempt to park operating liquidity in an offshore EMI and pay mainland tax liabilities or payroll from it will fail AML and tax review and can trigger downgrade of the WFOE to B/C class trade status.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In mainland China, the statutory legal representative and at least one senior authorized signatory must appear physically in the branch for opening the RMB basic deposit account and provisioning banking tokens; remote consular proxy is not accepted for first onboarding. The Taiwan shareholder's legal representative may appoint a mainland-resident local director or branch manager, but the appointment requires a notarized power of attorney and a board resolution. Once the basic account is live, FX capital and trade accounts can be opened remotely by the same authorized person using the approved seal set and business license. Banks generally permit videoconference interviews for supplementary accounts but not for the initial basic-account interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership chain opacity: the Taiwan investor is a holding company with multiple legal entities; a purely paper chain cannot demonstrate ultimate beneficial ownership or source of funding, and the bank suspicious activity filing is triggered.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a bilingual legalized group ownership map from the Taiwanese investor through each incorporated intermediary to the individual UBOs; notarized board resolution of the Taiwan investor authorizing the WFOE capital commitment; audited financial statements of the investor for the last three fiscal years; twelve-month bank statements of the investing entity showing accumulation of surplus; UBO passports, address verification and AML self-declaration under mainland AML rules; and SAFE FDI registration receipt where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The inbound capital injection is proposed from a Taiwan bank in a currency other than the approved equity contribution or via a payment aggregator that is not the registered shareholder, creating a third-party payment red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a registry-perfect capital remittance plan in which the remitter exactly matches the SAFE-registered Taiwan shareholder; SWIFT MT103 fields 50K, 56A and 59A reference the WFOE FDI registration code; foreign exchange purchase and sale contract with purpose code for foreign direct investment equity contribution; original capital commitment schedule; bank release letter; and a pre-transaction source-of-funds audit file containing payroll, vendor and dividend trails from a licensed Taiwan bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital software and CRM subscription revenue may be commingled with affiliate service fees and data-centre charges, so banks cannot determine whether current-account entries are genuine trade transactions or disguised capital transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the master service agreement and order forms for each customer tenant; itemised invoicing and settlement statements from Stripe Billing and Direct Debit; server and cloud resource consumption logs mapped to revenue; transfer pricing documentation for the Taiwan group; VAT and corporate income tax filing receipts; and an independent accountant's report on revenue recognition method.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-control and sanctions screening failure: the vertical ERP and CRM software may contain analytics features with potential dual-use or restricted-party end-user exposure, and internet-based payment routing makes dormant sanctions exposure difficult to exclude.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a product ECCN classification certificate showing EAR99 status where applicable; consolidated counterparty and beneficial-owner sanctions and PEP screening reports from a reputable third-party database; end-user certificates for the largest customer accounts; contractual territorial and data usage clauses; no-denied-party declarations from customers; and a written export compliance policy approved by the WFOE board.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Complete the Taiwan-side investment approval if required, then perform SAFE FDI registration through a designated bank and obtain the FDI registration voucher. Open a foreign currency capital settlement account at a Tier-1 domestic bank with SAFE transaction purpose code for foreign direct investment paid-in capital. The Taiwan parent must remit from its own corporate account using SWIFT MT103; the remitter must be the registered shareholder and the beneficiary must be the WFOE. Deposit the incoming funds, then convert to RMB using payment-purpose settlement with supporting board resolution, contract and the bank's capital-account FX payment confirmation. For RMB inbound investment, route through CIPS using a Taiwan participating bank or the cross-strait RMB clearing bank while preserving the same FDI registration reference. After funds are credited, engage a licensed Chinese CPA to issue a capital verification report and record paid-in capital in the National Enterprise Credit Information System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for cross-border vendor payments, software partner fees, cloud infrastructure costs, intercompany recharges and dividends after tax clearance; message fields must carry the SAFE purpose code for computer and information services or operational expenses. For high-value hardware or equipment procurement, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600 with negotiation through a Taiwan or Singapore bank. For recurring lower-risk trade settlements, use documentary collections in the form of documents against payment or documents against acceptance. All cross-border RMB settlements to Taiwan counterparties can be cleared via CIPS and CNAPS through the cross-strait RMB clearing bank. Domestic customer collections via Direct Debit or Stripe Billing aggregator settlement must be reconciled to the main FX settlement account and reported to the bank with subscription contract evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts executed with a SAFE-licensed onshore bank under a real current-account invoice backlog, with maturity not exceeding 12 months.

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for rebalancing USD operating liquidity against RMB funding, provided the notional matches SAFE-registered services or trade exposures and the bank has NAFMII or ISDA master documentation.
Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options and collars used to hedge specific contract or intercompany invoices; speculative, barrier or exotic knockout structures are not permitted.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for the WFOE are not a permissible onshore hedging rail; if the Taiwan parent wishes to hedge group-level RMB risk, it must book the NDF offshore in its own name with no subsidiary guarantee or margin support from the WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Transparency / Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Information Platform, Taiwan (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 January following each fiscal year end, being within 15 days after the fiscal year-end, with re-confirmation within 15 days after any change in directors, managers, supervisors, or shareholders holding 10 percent or more of the shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA issues a correction order; continued default attracts administrative fines up to NT$500,000 (approximately US$15,600); if the company remains non-operative for six consecutive months, MOEA may administratively dissolve or revoke the registration under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Various Income Withholding Statement Filing (Annual Withholding and Non-withholding Statement, Form/File to Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar tax year for all income paid, deducted, and withheld during the previous year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or misreporting attracts statutory late-filing and omission penalties under the Income Tax Act (generally 10 percent of the under-reported withholding amount plus interest); prolonged non-compliance may trigger tax lien, compulsory execution, and tax registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular Value-Added Business Tax Return (Two-Month Statutory Cycle Repeated Annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every two-month filing period: Jan-Feb due 15 Mar; Mar-Apr due 15 May; May-Jun due 15 Jul; Jul-Aug due 15 Sep; Sep-Oct due 15 Nov; Nov-Dec due 15 Jan of the following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Value-Added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, late filing and understatement attract late-filing fines and a 15 percent surcharge on the understated tax amount, plus overdue interest; repeated serious violations may lead to cancellation of tax registration and business closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Undistributed Retained Earnings Surtax Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May through 31 May following the close of the fiscal year; if a special accounting period is adopted, within the fifth month after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior investigation triggers a 10 percent additional tax on the payable amount; failure to file triggers a 15 percent additional tax plus interest under the Income Tax Act and Tax Collection Act; unpaid taxes become a statutory lien and are enforced by compulsory execution, and continued non-operation for six months permits MOEA administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Final Accounts, and Shareholder Approval Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office for shareholder inspection; audited financial statements are retained for regulatory inspection and submitted with the income tax filing to the National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final accounts and financial statements must be completed and approved within six months after fiscal year-end, in any event before the profit-seeking enterprise income tax filing deadline; a written shareholder resolution is permissible for a limited liability WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or approve statutory financial statements exposes responsible directors to administrative fines under the Company Act; knowingly false statements may attract criminal liability; failure to obtain a required CPA audit above the NT$30 million paid-in-capital threshold triggers MOEA corrective orders and fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA financial statement audit regulations, a Taiwan private WFOE whose paid-in capital reaches or exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately US$940,000) must have its annual financial statements audited and certified by an independent certified public accountant. Public companies, financial institutions, insurance companies, securities and futures enterprises are compulsorily audited regardless of that threshold; there is no ordinary balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount trigger for a non-public Taiwan WFOE below the paid-in capital threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public Taiwan WFOEs prepare accounts under the Taiwan Business Accounting Act and the Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Standards (EAS/ECS local GAAP); public companies and FSC-regulated institutions apply Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; group reporting may require reconciliation to the parent company's PRC accounting standards or IFRS framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1 requires every company, including a foreign-invested WFOE, to file its corporate transparency data on the MOEA Company Registration Information Platform within 15 days after each fiscal year-end, i.e. by 15 January annually, and to re-file within 15 days of any change in directors, managers, supervisors, or shareholders holding

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (profit-seeking enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000 are exempt from profit-seeking enterprise income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D investment tax credit equal to 15% of eligible R&D expenditure, creditable against up to 30% of the otherwise payable corporate income tax under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; accelerated depreciation for smart machinery and 5G-related assets; 5% surtax on undistributed retained earnings under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act; Alternative Minimum Tax at 12% of taxable base under the Income Basic Tax Act.
